    <bpmn:endEvent id="EndEvent_BotFinished" name="Bot finished and shared"/>

        <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MessageDef_UpdateList" messageRef="Msg_UpdateList"/>

      <bpmn:userTask id="UserTask_UpdateList" name="Update list of materials to farm"/>
      <bpmn:endEvent id="EndEvent_ListUpdated" name="List updated"/>
      <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_16" sourceRef="StartEvent_UpdateList" targetRef="UserTask_UpdateList"/>
      <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_17" sourceRef="UserTask_UpdateList" targetRef="EndEvent_ListUpdated"/>

      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">${bragToFriends}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_08" sourceRef="Gateway_Share_Split" targetRef="SendTask_SendMaterials">

    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_09" sourceRef="SendTask_Brag" targetRef="Gateway_Share_Join"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_10" sourceRef="SendTask_SendMaterials" targetRef="Gateway_Share_Join"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_11" sourceRef="Gateway_Share_Join" targetRef="EndEvent_BotFinished"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_12" sourceRef="BoundaryEvent_Disaster" targetRef="ServiceTask_Recover"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_15" sourceRef="SendTask_NotifyMilestone" targetRef="EndEvent_MilestoneNotified"/>
  </bpmn:process>

rules.instruction: When the description says that several items can be processed at the same time (in parallel, up to a stated limit), and each item then needs its own input step before a shared activity can continue: Model a parallel gateway split placed before the per-item input task so that each item's input branch starts in parallel, and join those branches with a parallel gateway before the shared continuation. Do not replace the split with an exclusive gateway, and do not sequence the item inputs one after another unless the description orders them.
rules.situation: the description says that several items can be processed at the same time (in parallel, up to a stated limit), and each item then needs its own input step before a shared activity can continue

rules.instruction: When the description names a work activity with its own verb and object, and a generated task label would use a different verb, a synonym, a restated object, or extra words such as a recipient, a reaction, or a circumstance that the description does not attach to that activity's own action: Label the task with the verb and object words that the description uses for that activity, in the same order and without synonyms or added qualifiers. Model any circumstance, reaction, or recipient that the description states separately as an event, a gateway branch, or the sequence flow leading to the task.
rules.situation: the description names a work activity with its own verb and object, and a generated task label would use a different verb, a synonym, a restated object, or extra words such as a recipient, a reaction, or a circumstance that the description does not attach to that activity's own action

rules.instruction: When the description has one human actor who states choices and then creates or configures an automated helper, and that same helper later performs its own stated activities within the same flow, rather than only exchanging messages with the actor: Model one participant pool that contains the whole flow, with one lane for the human actor and one lane for the helper. Place the actor's steps (stating choices, configuring the helper) in the actor's lane, and place the helper's own activities in the helper's lane. Use a single start event for the flow, located in the lane of the actor who initiates it, and connect steps across lanes with sequence flows. Do not add a separate start event for the helper's setup, and do not place the helper in its own pool.
rules.situation: the description has one human actor who states choices and then creates or configures an automated helper, and that same helper later performs its own stated activities within the same flow, rather than only exchanging messages with the actor

rules.instruction: When the description says a bounded number of items (up to N) can be handled in parallel, each item receiving its own work, and does not say they are handled one after another: Model the simultaneous handling as a parallel gateway that splits the flow into one branch per item, where each branch performs the work for its item, followed by a parallel gateway that joins the branches before the next described step. Do not model the simultaneous work as a single sequential task or a loop, and do not put decision conditions on these parallel branches.
rules.situation: the description says a bounded number of items (up to N) can be handled in parallel, each item receiving its own work, and does not say they are handled one after another

rules.instruction: When the description states that some resources must first be obtained in order to produce an intermediate means (such as a tool), and that this means is then used to gather other resources, so a production dependency chain is stated: Model the production of the intermediate means as its own task placed before the gathering task that uses it, connected by a sequence flow. Keep the separately described gathering of the items as distinct tasks, and do not fold the production step into the later gathering activity.
rules.situation: the description states that some resources must first be obtained in order to produce an intermediate means (such as a tool), and that this means is then used to gather other resources, so a production dependency chain is stated

rules.instruction: Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
rules.situation: the description states that an activity is carried out by an actor or automated participant itself, and it names no external service, API, or system call for that activity

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity may also be performed as an optional extra step, on top of the main path, so it is not performed in every case (signalled by wording such as 'may also'): Place an exclusive gateway on the path at the point where the optional activity could occur. Give the optional activity its own outgoing sequence flow from that gateway, and give a bypass flow that skips it. Merge the optional branch and the bypass with an exclusive gateway before the next described step. Keep the required activities on the main path unconditional and do not drop the optional activity.
rules.situation: the description states that a response or notification to an occurrence happens only on some occasions, while the other steps of the process continue unchanged in every case, so the response is not performed in every run

rules.instruction: When the description states that a person must first determine or choose which items they want before any automated process step (such as starting work or collecting) takes place: Model the step where the person determines or chooses their items as a user task performed by that person, placed before the automated activities that depend on the choice. Do not model it as a service, script or generic task, and do not leave it implicit in the start of the automated work.
rules.situation: the description states that a person must first determine or choose which items they want before any automated process step (such as starting work or collecting) takes place

rules.instruction: When the description says the process begins when a participant's need or condition arises (a state the participant notices or is in), and the performed actions that follow are described separately: Model the start event with a label that names the arising condition as a state, in the description's wording, rather than the participant's later action or a generic 'participant performs X' phrase. Keep the participant's performed actions as tasks placed after the start event, and do not use the start event label to stand for those actions.
rules.situation: the description says the process begins when a participant's wish or desire arises, and the participant's later steps are described separately as work in the same lane
